title: CReal.supOn exists as a total, axiom-free CReal function -- the supremum value of a uniformly continuous function on [a, b]
statement: There is a total function CReal.supOn taking a function F, endpoints a <= b, and a witness that F is uniformly continuous on [a,b], and returning a CReal -- the limit of the sequence of finite mesh maxima (CReal.supSeq), built as a CReal.mk with a regularity proof. Admitted by the trusted kernel gate with an empty axiom footprint. This is the supremum VALUE only: CReal.supOn_ub and CReal.supOn_approx_lub (registered separately) are what CHARACTERIZE it as a supremum, and CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign proves the exact form (an attaining maximiser) is unavailable from these hypotheses alone.

formal.statement: def CReal.supOn : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal.le x1 x2) -> ((x4 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x1 x2) -> CReal)))))

evidence.supports: CReal.supOn is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration CReal.supOn --require-kind definition 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^found[[:space:]]creal[[:space:]]definition[[:space:]]CReal\.supOn[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: CReal.supOn is a Declaration::Definition, not a Theorem, and every in-tree theorem inventory (theorem_dependency_inventory, prelude_theorem_inventory, nat_theorem_inventory) deliberately excludes Definitions. kernel_declaration_projection's '--require-declaration <name> --require-kind <kind>' searches every constructed prelude's environment for an EXACT display-name match of the given kind and exits non-zero on no match, so a deleted or renamed CReal.supOn cannot read as present. This is the same route ADR-0692 used to independently re-derive that CReal.supOn exists (as opposed to CReal.supOn_upper_bound, a name that never existed) -- see that ADR and ADR-0895 for the history of why this fact was absent from the ledger until now despite the declaration itself having landed earlier. --release is MANDATORY: this tool also builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the creal prelude's trusted surface is empty, which bounds CReal.supOn
evidence.notes: Re-measured on this tree: creal: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0, exits 0 printing 'ok: creal trusted surface = 0'. That bounds every declaration in the creal environment, including CReal.supOn, since a declaration cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. --require-axiom-free <name> errors for a prelude never built by this run. --release is MANDATORY here.

provenance.source: canonical type read via kernel_declaration_projection's own UNFILTERED emit mode (cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection, no --require-declaration flag) on this lane's own worktree build, filtered to the creal-prelude row for this declaration.

notes: depends_on is empty because the construction's own direct building blocks (CReal.supSeq, CReal.speedup, CReal.mk, CReal.regular_of_scaled_cauchy) are either plain Definitions or unregistered internal theorems, matching CReal.integral's own depends_on rationale. CReal.supOn landed before this lane (ADR-0691); this fact registers a construction that already existed but that ZERO facts named -- ADR-0692 measured this gap directly. The propositions ABOUT this construction are the separate facts F:creal-supon-ub, F:creal-supon-approx-lub, and F:creal-evt-approx-max.
